scopeNotes: Four imported spelling and date variants broadly cover northern Fennoscandia and the Kola region. Their exact boundaries and the earliest 200 CE ethnic label are not certified.
Sámi, the North American Samish and the South American Pisamira are distinct identities despite similar strings in a search.
The late ninth-century report is attributed to Ottarr. No unqualified identification of Tacitus’s Fenni or every early northern population is adopted.
Intensive herding chronology and milk production describe regional practices. They do not imply that all Sámi were nomads or that herding began everywhere at one date.
Swedish sources were read in Swedish. Their national school and border histories are not generalized as identical policies in Russia, Norway and Finland.
Tirro Farm and Mirhamintupa are named museum structures. A general discussion of náhppi vessels is not described as an excavation or a dated museum specimen.
Siida’s earlier archaeological layers are not automatically assigned Sámi ethnicity. The 1963 museum opening is separate from its 1959 foundation.
Parliaments began operating in different years; the card avoids conflating enabling legislation, first meetings and a single pan-Sámi state.
Independent review, geometry assessment and depth certification remain pending. No modern country is assigned as the people’s successor.
